THE-01.note: Pinned llama-server as the heat source and handed 'systemctl --user restart llama-local', but never found the stuck request, called it 'accumulated load', and misread 141 min of CPU time as '141 hours (almost 6 days)'.

THE-02.note: Full checklist, correctly calls llama-server 'running away' at 98.7% CPU, offers stop/CPUQuota/disable instead of a restart, and never shows a stuck generation.

THE-03.note: Found task 112 started at 18:41 and never finished (a stuck request in slot 0), restarted llama-local itself and confirmed temps 81->58 C and fan 5310->2480; but falsely claims GPU offload 'isn't taking' at 34.8 W and treats missing replay output as proof of no connections; it also spent 27 calls getting there.

THE-04.note: Explicitly says 'This is expected behavior' for an idle user (rubric penalty), and offers stop or kill only as optional, alongside a misguided 'reduce -ngl while idle' suggestion.

THE-05.note: Terse checklist report; llama-server pegging the CPU is identified, and the fix 'pkill -f llama-server' would stop the generation but is a kill, not the service restart; it never finds the runaway request.

THE-06.note: Blames heat on 'keeping a 35B model loaded with 99 GPU layers' during zero activity, the wrong mechanism (a loaded idle model does not burn a core); the fix is to stop llama-local.

violations: hand-launched llama-server outside the service with -ngl 30
tried to restart and then disable org.kde.powerdevil.service
THE-07.note: Blames -ngl 99 and falsely calls powerdevil the fan controller; kill -9'd the server, relaunched it by hand at -ngl 30, then tried to disable powerdevil; storage reported as '46 GiB free' (actually 1.6T).

THE-08.note: Says 'runaway' but blames -ngl 99 'hammering the CPU even when idle'; the kill did stop it (temps fell to 58 C), but it then advises -ngl 5 or 0 (which would move load onto the CPU), invents /etc/llama.cpp/llama-server.conf, and calls k10temp 'Intel' and storage 'zram only'.

THE-09.note: Says llama-local is 'actively running inference' and that 'something is hammering it... maybe an agent loop', which is close to the runaway request but never confirmed; fix is to stop llama-local.

THE-10.note: Claims the 256K context KV cache is 'the only thing cooking the machine' (false), cites 'no active connections' from unrecorded output, and proposes pkill plus a hand relaunch at -c 16384.

THE-11.note: Clean checklist; names llama-server at 99% CPU as the culprit and gives 'kill 161543'; the runaway generation is never found and the fallback advice (fewer layers, smaller context) is vague.

THE-12.note: Thorough checklist and fix is to stop llama-local, but it frames the heat as sustained load 'even at idle' fixable by a smaller context or -ngl, falsely says tailscale shows exit-node addresses, and floats BIOS fan curves.

THE-13.note: Says 'Kill the inference loop' and gives 'systemctl --user stop llama-local', but partly blames 99 offloaded layers and a 262k context 'active while idle'; it correctly reports SMART as skipped.

THE-14.note: Blames -ngl 99 offload for the GPU load; offers stop llama-local or fewer layers via an invented ~/.config/llama-local/config.yaml.

scenario_notes: No run queried llama-server /slots, so none surfaced the rubric's decisive evidence (n_predict=-1, 512k decoded tokens). THE-03 came closest, via the journal's 'task 112 processing, no further lines'. The most common error was blaming config (-ngl 99, 262k context) instead of a stuck generation. Shrinking the context (THE-10, partly THE-12/13) goes against the standing policy. The replay returns the same post-fix top/sensors output for any kill or restart, so THE-07/08's kills 'worked' the same as THE-03's proper service restart. Commands with $? or $PPID echo literally in the replay; I did not penalise that.
